welcome.title: Welcome to CORTAI Sentry
welcome.summary: What the operator console is for, and where to begin.
welcome.body:
CORTAI Sentry is the console a remote-monitoring operator uses to watch client sites, handle alarms and deter intruders through cameras, speakers, sirens and strobes. One operator works one desk and handles **up to three incidents at the same time**, each in its own *lane*.

## What you do here

- **Take** alarms from the queue, highest priority first.
- **Watch** the live camera and the evidence the system captured.
- **Respond**: talk down, arm the siren or strobe, call the keyholder, request police dispatch.
- **Close** each incident with a short memo that the site owner reads.

## What the console does for you

- Sorts the queue by priority, then by how long each alarm has waited.
- Runs the **response ladder**: it moves each incident to the next step by itself unless you halt it.
- Counts how long each lane has gone without your attention and pages the desk supervisor at 01:00.
- Writes everything you do to the incident timeline. The shift report is built from that timeline, not from what you type.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Two things never happen on their own: **police dispatch** always needs your confirmation, and a **fourth lane** is always refused. Both rules protect the quality of your attention.

## Where to start

1. Read [The console at a glance](#console-overview) to learn the screen.
2. Follow [Your first alarm](#first-alarm) end to end.
3. Keep [Keyboard shortcuts](#keyboard-shortcuts) at hand. Press [[Shift+?]] at any time to see them on screen.

> [!TIP]
> Press [[F1]] anywhere in the console. Help opens on the article for what is on your screen right now.

console-overview.title: The console at a glance
console-overview.summary: The five areas of the screen and what each one is for.
console-overview.body:
The console is one screen with five fixed areas. Nothing important hides behind menus: every lane, the queue and the health of the estate stay visible while you work.

{{fig:console-overview}}

## Top bar

The logo dot shows the state of the whole desk: blue when idle, amber with an open incident, red when a lane has been unattended for 60 seconds, grey when the console is offline. Next to it you see your shift, the desk number and the time left on shift.

The search box opens the [command palette](#command-palette) ([[Ctrl+K]] or [[⌘+K]]). The pills show open lanes, cameras online, camera faults and alarms waiting; each pill is also a shortcut to the matching view.

## Left panel

Three tabs: **Estate** (every site and camera, see [Estate panel and site tree](#estate-panel)), **Watch** (sites with unusual patterns, see [Watch list](#watch-list)) and **History** (incidents closed this shift, see [History and incident records](#incident-records)).

## Lane workspace

The large centre area always shows **one** lane: the focused one. Video, evidence and timeline sit on the left; everything you can decide or do sits on the right. See [The lane workspace](#lane-workspace).

## Right rail

**Peripheral lanes**: the other open lanes as compact cards with live video and an unattended timer. Free lanes appear as dashed slots. Below them is the **queue** of waiting alarms.

## Status bar

Clock, lanes, queue, where the microphone is, active sirens, and a reminder of the most used keys.

> [!NOTE]
> On smaller screens the same areas rearrange. See [Layouts on different screens](#screen-sizes).

sign-in.title: Sign in and choose a desk
sign-in.summary: Sign in with your operator ID or email and password, pick your desk, and start with no lanes open.
sign-in.body:
Every shift starts on the sign-in screen. There is no single sign-on or social login: you sign in with the operator ID or work email and password your desk supervisor gave you.

{{fig:sign-in}}

## Sign in

1. Enter your **Operator ID or email**, for example OP-214.
2. Enter your **Password**. Select the eye button to check what you typed. If Caps Lock is on, a warning appears under the field.
3. Choose your **Desk** (1 to 4). The desk decides which supervisor is paged for your lanes.
4. Select **Sign in** or press [[Enter]].

## What you see next

The console loads for a moment, then opens with **no lanes open** and **no camera selected**. The right rail shows three empty lane slots: slot A offers to take the next alarm, B and C open in turn. A message confirms your desk.

{{fig:empty-console}}

Press [[T]] or select **Take next** to start working. See [Take the next alarm](#take-alarm).

> [!NOTE]
> Every sign-in, failed attempt and sign-out is logged with the workstation and desk.

## Sign out

Select your avatar in the top bar, or run **Sign out** from the command palette. You can sign out only when **no lanes are open**: close or hand off each lane first. If you step away for a short time, lock the console instead (see [Console locked](#lock-screen)).

first-alarm.title: Your first alarm, end to end
first-alarm.summary: A walk-through of one incident: take it, look, respond, write the memo, close.
first-alarm.body:
This walk-through uses the most common case: a person is seen somewhere they should not be, after hours.

1. **Take it.** Press [[T]]. The top alarm in the queue opens in lane {{lane:A}} and becomes the focused lane. The video connects in about two seconds.
2. **Read the header.** Site, priority (for example {{prio:P1}}), what triggered the alarm and which camera saw it.
3. **Look before you act.** Check the live video, then the **Evidence** stills. Stills marked **AI** were flagged by the model. The **Why P1** box lists the factors that raised the priority; the model's confidence is one input, not the verdict.
4. **Talk down.** Hold [[Space]], speak, release. Your words go to the site speaker and are written to the transcript. See [Talk to people on site](#talk-down).
5. **Escalate if needed.** Hold [[S]] for 600 ms to arm the siren. The response ladder also moves on by itself: talk-down, siren, keyholder, then dispatch, which always waits for you. See [Run the response ladder](#response-ladder).
6. **Write notes as you go.** Press [[N]], type what you see, press [[Enter]].
7. **Close.** Press [[E]], write at least 40 characters on what happened and how it ended, choose the outcome and any follow-ups, then **Close incident**. See [Close an incident](#close-incident).

The lane is free again. If alarms are waiting, the confirmation offers **Take next** straight away.

> [!TIP]
> While you work in one lane, keep an eye on the cards in the right rail. A lane you have not looked at for 30 seconds turns amber. Press its letter ([[A]], [[B]] or [[C]]) to look at it.

screen-sizes.title: Layouts on different screens
screen-sizes.summary: How the console adapts to desktop, laptop and touch tablet screens.
screen-sizes.body:
The console is designed for a control-room display, 1920 × 1080 or larger. It keeps working on smaller screens by moving panels, never by hiding a lane.

| Screen | Width | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| Desktop | 1440 px and wider | All five areas are visible at once. |
| Laptop | 1024–1439 px | The left panel becomes an icon rail. Estate, Watch and History open as a drawer over the workspace; Camera wall, Shift report, Help and Settings move from the top bar into the rail. |
| Tablet and touch | below 1024 px, or any touch screen | A lane switcher sits under the top bar; a bottom bar holds Console, Queue, Sites, Wall, Report, Help and Settings. Dialogs open as sheets from the bottom. Controls grow to at least 44 px. |

## Laptop

{{fig:laptop-layout}}

Select an icon in the rail to open its drawer. Select anywhere outside the drawer, or press [[Esc]], to close it. The drawer never blocks the lane timers: they keep running.

## Tablet and touch

{{fig:tablet-layout}}

Single-key shortcuts still work with a keyboard attached. Without one, **hold** the Siren and Strobe buttons for 600 ms, and hold **Talk-down** to speak.

take-alarm.title: Take the next alarm
take-alarm.summary: Move the top alarm from the queue into a free lane.
take-alarm.body:
Alarms wait in the **Queue** in the right rail, sorted by priority and then by how long they have waited. You take them one at a time into a free lane.

## Take the top alarm

1. Check that a lane is free: the rail shows a dashed **Lane … free** slot, and the top bar reads less than 3/3.
2. Press [[T]], or select **Take next**.

The alarm opens in the first free lane (A, then B, then C) and becomes the focused lane. The video shows **Connecting** for about two seconds, the response ladder starts at step 1 and the timeline records who took it and how long it waited.

## Take a specific alarm

1. Select the alarm in the queue to highlight it. The [[T]] hint moves to that item.
2. Press [[T]], or select its **Take** button.

Use this when you know the site, or when a lower-priority alarm is clearly more urgent than its label.

## Filter the queue

Select **P1–P2** to see only critical and high alarms. **All** shows everything. Filtering never changes the order.

> [!WARNING]
> With three lanes open, taking a fourth is refused. See [Lane limit reached](#lane-limit).

> [!NOTE]
> A new P1 or P2 alarm shows a short message even when you are busy in a lane. P3 and P4 arrive quietly in the queue.

lane-workspace.title: The lane workspace
lane-workspace.summary: Every part of the focused lane: video, evidence, timeline, ladder, actions and notes.
lane-workspace.body:
The workspace shows the focused lane. Its color strip and letter match the lane key, so you always know which incident you are acting on.

{{fig:lane-workspace}}

## Watch column

- **Video.** Live picture with the camera name, the time, the site and the stream quality in the corners. The box around a person or vehicle shows what the model detected and its confidence.
- **Evidence.** Six stills captured around the alarm. Select one to see it in the video area; **AI** marks stills the model flagged.
- **Timeline, Transcript, Notes.** The timeline lists every system event and everything you did. The transcript holds what you said and what the site microphone picked up. Notes shows only your notes.

## Decide column

- **Response ladder.** The next escalation step and how long until it starts. See [Run the response ladder](#response-ladder).
- **Actions.** Talk-down, Siren and Strobe. See [Talk to people on site](#talk-down) and [Use the siren and strobe](#siren-strobe).
- **Why P1.** The factors behind the priority, strongest first.
- **Add note.** Type and press [[Enter]]. See [Add notes](#add-notes).
- **Close incident** ([[E]]).

## Header tools

- **Focus mode** ([[F]]) hides the side panels so the video gets the whole width. Press [[F]] again to bring them back.
- **Hand off** passes the lane to the desk supervisor. See [Hand off a lane](#hand-off).

## Microphone dock

The strip at the bottom shows where the microphone is. It lives on one lane at a time. See [Talk to people on site](#talk-down).

switch-lanes.title: Switch between lanes
switch-lanes.summary: Look at another open lane without losing anything in the first one.
switch-lanes.body:
Only one lane is in the workspace at a time. Switching is instant and safe: timers, sirens and the ladder keep running in every lane.

## Switch

- Press the lane letter: [[A]], [[B]] or [[C]].
- Or select the lane's card in the right rail.
- On a touch screen, use the lane switcher under the top bar.

The lane you leave becomes a card in the right rail and starts counting **unattended** time. The lane you open resets its unattended timer to zero.

{{fig:peripheral-card}}

## Read a lane card

The card shows the site, the priority, a small live video, the ladder step as four dots and the **Unattended** meter. The meter fills over 60 seconds: amber from 30 s, red at 60 s when the supervisor is paged.

> [!TIP]
> Switch before a card turns red. A quick look is enough: the moment a lane is on screen, its unattended timer resets.

> [!NOTE]
> The microphone does not follow you when you switch. Press [[M]] to move it to the lane you are looking at.

talk-down.title: Talk to people on site
talk-down.summary: Speak through the site speaker with push-to-talk, and move the microphone between lanes.
talk-down.body:
Talk-down is usually the first and most effective deterrent. The console uses **push-to-talk**: the site hears you only while you hold the key or button.

## Speak

1. Check the microphone dock at the bottom of the workspace. It should read **Mic on this lane**.
2. Hold [[Space]], or press and hold **Talk-down**.
3. Speak. The level meter moves with your voice and the dock reads **Live to site speaker**.
4. Release to stop.

Each talk-down is written to the timeline with its length, and to the **Transcript** tab.

## Move the microphone

The microphone belongs to one lane (or one camera) at a time, so you never speak to the wrong site. If the dock reads **Mic is on lane B**, Talk-down is disabled here.

1. Press [[M]], or select **Move mic here**.
2. Hold [[Space]] to speak.

> [!TIP]
> Keep it short and specific: say they are on camera, what they must do and what happens next. Suggested lines are in the site procedures.

> [!NOTE]
> The transcript is an aid, not evidence. The audio recording is kept as recorded.

siren-strobe.title: Use the siren and strobe
siren-strobe.summary: Arm and stop the site siren and strobe with a deliberate 600 ms hold.
siren-strobe.body:
Sirens and strobes are loud and visible to neighbours, so they need a **hold** to arm. A stray key press never starts one.

{{fig:actions}}

## Arm

1. Press and hold [[S]] for the siren or [[L]] for the strobe. You can also press and hold the button.
2. Keep holding: the button fills and reads **Keep holding…**.
3. After 600 ms the device arms. The button reads **ON** with a running time.

Let go early to cancel. Nothing is sent.

## Stop

Press the button (or the key) once. A single press stops a running siren or strobe; no hold is needed.

## What else starts a siren

The [response ladder](#response-ladder) arms the siren by itself when it reaches step 2 (**Siren**). You can stop it the same way.

> [!WARNING]
> On a camera without an incident (see [Watch a camera without an incident](#camera-view)), the siren and strobe stop as soon as you leave that camera. In a lane they keep running until you stop them or close the incident.

response-ladder.title: Run the response ladder
response-ladder.summary: Let the ladder escalate on its own, halt it while you handle things, and confirm dispatch.
response-ladder.body:
Each lane has a four-step response ladder. It advances by itself on a timer so that an incident keeps moving even when your attention is elsewhere.

{{fig:ladder}}

| Step | What happens | Moves on after |
|---|---|---|
| 1 · Talk-down | You speak to the site. | 30 s |
| 2 · Siren | The siren arms automatically. | 45 s |
| 3 · Keyholder | A call to the site's keyholder is queued. | 60 s |
| 4 · Dispatch | Waits for you: **Confirm dispatch** or close. | never on its own |

## Halt the ladder

When you are handling the situation and do not want the next step to fire, press [[H]] or select **Halt**. The badge reads {{badge:b-warn|Halted}} and the timer stops.

## Resume

Press [[R]] or select **Resume**. The timer continues from where it stopped.

## Confirm dispatch

At step 4 the badge reads **Needs confirm**. Select **Confirm dispatch** to request police. The timeline records the request and its reference. If the situation is over, close the incident instead.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Dispatch is never automatic. For P3 and P4 alarms the dispatch step is shown dimmed: it is available, but rarely right.

> [!NOTE]
> When a lane you are not looking at moves to Keyholder or Dispatch, a message tells you which lane and site.

add-notes.title: Add notes
add-notes.summary: Write short observations to the incident timeline while you work.
add-notes.body:
Notes are short, timestamped observations. They end up in the incident record and help whoever reads it later.

1. Press [[N]], or select the **Add note** field.
2. Type what you see or what you did.
3. Press [[Enter]].

The note appears in the timeline with the time, and in the **Notes** tab. The field clears and stays ready for the next note.

> [!TIP]
> Write facts, not conclusions: "Second person approached the passenger side, left on foot" is more useful than "suspicious".

Notes typed while the console is offline are kept on this workstation and sent when the connection returns. See [Connection lost](#connection-lost).

close-incident.title: Close an incident
close-incident.summary: Write the closeout memo, choose the outcome and follow-ups, and free the lane.
close-incident.body:
Closing takes three short steps. The memo and timeline go to the site owner, and the record is sealed.

## 1 · Closeout memo

1. Press [[E]], or select **Close incident**.
2. Check the recap: how long the lane was open, how many actions you took, the ladder step and the siren time.
3. Write **what happened and how it ended**, at least 40 characters. Use the **Insert** chips for common endings.
4. Select **Next steps**, or press [[Ctrl+Enter]] ([[⌘+Enter]] on a Mac).

{{fig:close-step1}}

## 2 · Outcome and next steps

1. Choose the **Outcome**: Resolved, False alarm or Referred to police.
2. Tick the **follow-ups** to schedule: notify the keyholder at 07:00, request a plate lookup, book a patrol pass, flag the camera for an angle review.
3. Select **Close incident**.

{{fig:close-step2}}

## 3 · Done

The confirmation shows the lane is free and how many follow-ups were scheduled. If alarms are waiting, select **Take next** or press [[T]].

## After closing

- The incident moves to **History** as a sealed, read-only record. See [History and incident records](#incident-records).
- The microphone moves to another open lane if it was on this one.
- The focus moves to the open lane that has waited longest.

> [!NOTE]
> Select **Back** in step 2 to edit the memo. Select **Cancel** or press [[Esc]] in step 1 to leave the lane open.

hand-off.title: Hand off a lane
hand-off.summary: Pass an open lane to the desk supervisor.
hand-off.body:
Hand off a lane when you need a free lane for something more urgent, when an incident needs a specialist, or at the end of your shift.

1. Focus the lane.
2. Select the **Hand off** button in the lane header (two arrows).
3. The timeline records **Hand-off requested** and a message confirms it.

The lane stays yours until the supervisor accepts. Keep watching it until then: its unattended timer still runs.

> [!NOTE]
> You cannot sign out while any lane is open. Hand off or close every lane first.

escalation.title: Respond to an unattended-lane escalation
escalation.summary: What the amber and red bars mean, and how to clear them.
escalation.body:
If a lane has not been on your screen for a while, the console warns you and then pages your desk supervisor.

{{fig:escalation-bar}}

| Unattended | What you see |
|---|---|
| 30 s | The lane card's meter turns amber. |
| 45 s | An amber bar under the top bar: "Supervisor is paged at 01:00 unless you look at the lane". |
| 60 s | The bar turns red, the supervisor is paged, a message appears and the logo dot turns red. |

## Clear it

- Press the lane's letter, or select **Go to lane …** in the bar. Looking at the lane resets its timer and clears the bar.

## Acknowledge without switching

When the bar is red and you cannot switch right now (for example, you are mid-talk-down in another lane), press [[K]] or select **Acknowledge**. The supervisor is informed that you know. The bar clears for good when you look at the lane.

> [!WARNING]
> Unattended time also counts while the console window is hidden behind another application, even for the focused lane.

> [!TIP]
> In a prototype session, press [[Shift+1]] to simulate an escalation on a peripheral lane.

estate-panel.title: Estate panel and site tree
estate-panel.summary: Find any site or camera, see its state, and open it.
estate-panel.body:
The **Estate** tab lists every site you monitor and its cameras.

{{fig:estate-panel}}

## Camera totals

The four counters at the top show how many cameras are **Live**, have **Motion**, have a stream **Fault**, or are **Offline**. See [Camera states](#camera-states).

## Open a site or camera

1. Select a site to expand it. A collapsed site shows lane badges (for example {{lane:A}}) if any of its cameras are in an open lane.
2. Select a camera:
   - If the camera belongs to an open lane, the console switches to that lane.
   - Otherwise it opens the camera on its own, without an incident. See [Watch a camera without an incident](#camera-view).

The camera you are watching is highlighted in the tree.

## On a laptop or tablet

On a laptop, select the building icon in the rail to open the Estate drawer. On a tablet, use **Sites** in the bottom bar.

camera-view.title: Watch a camera without an incident
camera-view.summary: Open any camera to look, talk or deter, without opening a lane.
camera-view.body:
Sometimes you want to look at a camera before anything has happened: a guard asked you to, the watch list flagged a site, or a neighbour camera is quiet. Camera view lets you do that without opening a lane.

{{fig:camera-view}}

## Open a camera

Select it in the site tree, on the camera wall, or in the **Site cameras** strip of another camera.

## What you can do

- **Look.** Live video, the other cameras on the same site, and the camera's log for this shift.
- **Talk and deter.** Talk-down, siren and strobe work as in a lane. Everything goes to the **site log**, not to an incident.
- **Write a note** to the site log.
- **Raise an incident** if you see something. See [Raise an incident from a camera](#raise-incident).

## Leave

Select **Back to lane …** or press [[Esc]]. You return to the lane you were on.

> [!WARNING]
> While you watch a camera, your open lanes keep counting unattended time. The siren and strobe on this camera stop when you leave it.

> [!NOTE]
> An offline camera opens with its last state and no actions: the speaker and deterrents on that device are unavailable.

raise-incident.title: Raise an incident from a camera
raise-incident.summary: Turn what you see on a camera into a lane with a priority you choose.
raise-incident.body:
When you see something on a camera that the analytics did not flag, raise the incident yourself.

1. Open the camera. See [Watch a camera without an incident](#camera-view).
2. Under **Raise incident**, choose the priority: {{prio:P1}}, {{prio:P2}}, {{prio:P3}} or {{prio:P4}}. P3 is preselected.
3. Select **Raise … incident**, or press [[I]].

The incident opens in the next free lane and becomes the focused lane. The camera's log, anything you said and any running siren or strobe move into the new incident, so nothing is lost. The response ladder starts at step 1.

> [!WARNING]
> With three lanes open, raising is refused. Close or hand off a lane first. See [Lane limit reached](#lane-limit).

camera-wall.title: Camera wall
camera-wall.summary: See every camera at once, filter by state and open any of them.
camera-wall.body:
The camera wall shows a tile for every camera, with cameras that need attention first.

{{fig:camera-wall}}

## Open the wall

Press [[W]], select the grid icon in the top bar (in the rail on a laptop), or select **Wall** in the bottom bar on a tablet.

## Filter

Use the tabs: **All**, **Live**, **Motion**, **Fault**, **Offline**. Each tab shows how many cameras it has. The grid scrolls; the tabs stay in place.

## Read a tile

- The top-left label shows the camera's state mark and name. See [Camera states](#camera-states).
- The footer shows the site, a lane badge if the camera is in an open lane, and the state in words.

## Open a camera

Select a tile. A camera that belongs to an open lane opens that lane; any other camera opens in camera view. The wall closes.

watch-list.title: Watch list
watch-list.summary: Sites with unusual activity patterns, ranked by a watch score.
watch-list.body:
The **Watch** tab highlights sites where recent activity looks unusual, even if no alarm has fired.

{{fig:watch-list}}

## Read a card

- **Score** from 0 to 100. Scores of 70 and above are highlighted.
- **Why**: the pattern behind the score, for example repeat visits over three nights.
- **Activity strip**: the last 24 hours, one bar per hour; darker means more activity.

Select a card to read the detail. Select it again to collapse it.

> [!NOTE]
> The model groups people by gait and clothing, not by face. The watch list is a prompt to look, not an alarm: nothing enters the queue from it.

incident-records.title: History and incident records
incident-records.summary: Find a closed incident and read its sealed record.
incident-records.body:
Every closed incident becomes a record. Records are read-only and sealed at closing.

## Find a record

1. Open the **History** tab in the left panel, or press [[/]] to jump straight to its search.
2. Type part of a site, camera, incident type or record number.
3. Narrow with **All**, **P1–P2** or **Referred**.

{{fig:history-list}}

The list is grouped by hour, newest first, and covers this shift; search reaches back seven days.

## Read a record

Select an item to open it.

{{fig:incident-record}}

| Tab | What it holds |
|---|---|
| Evidence | Stills and the clip. Stills and clip are hashed (SHA-256) at capture; exports keep the hash. |
| Timeline | Every event in order, with times. |
| Transcript | Operator speech and site audio, auto-transcribed. |
| Notes | The closeout memo, your notes and any addenda. |
| Operator | Who handled it, when, and who has viewed the record since. |

## Share or export

- **Copy link** copies a link to the record for colleagues with access.
- **Export PDF** creates a PDF for the client or the police.

> [!NOTE]
> Records are kept for 90 days. You cannot edit a sealed record; a supervisor can add an addendum.

shift-report.title: Shift report
shift-report.summary: Your shift in numbers, ready for the handover.
shift-report.body:
The shift report summarises your shift for the desk supervisor. All figures come from the timeline, not from anything you type.

{{fig:shift-report}}

## Open it

Press [[P]], select the document icon in the top bar (in the rail on a laptop), or select **Report** in the bottom bar on a tablet.

## What it shows

| Figure | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Closed | Incidents closed this shift, and how many are still open. |
| Median time to take | How long alarms waited before someone took them. Target: 00:30. |
| Median time to close | How long incidents stayed open. |
| Deterrent actions | Talk-downs, sirens and strobes. |
| Supervisor pages | Times a lane stayed unattended for 60 s. |

Below the figures: incidents by hour, and the list of closed incidents. Select a row to open its record.

## Hand it over

Select **Copy summary** and paste it into the handover note.

three-lanes.title: Lanes: the three-lane model
three-lanes.summary: Why an operator works in lanes, and why there are never more than three.
three-lanes.body:
A **lane** is one open incident: one site, one alarm, one response ladder, one timeline. Lanes are named {{lane:A}}, {{lane:B}} and {{lane:C}} and keep their letter and color until they close, so muscle memory works: [[A]] always takes you to the same incident.

## Focused and peripheral

- The **focused** lane fills the workspace. It is the only lane you act on with keys like [[Space]], [[S]] or [[E]].
- Every other open lane is **peripheral**: a card in the right rail with live video, the ladder step and an unattended timer.

## Why three

Handling several incidents at once is normal on a busy night. Past three, attention quality drops sharply: operators miss changes in peripheral video and react late to escalations. So the console refuses a fourth lane instead of letting quality degrade quietly.

When all three lanes are busy and a new P1 arrives, you choose what to let go: close a lane, or hand it off. See [Lane limit reached](#lane-limit).

## Lanes and the microphone

The microphone belongs to one lane at a time, independent of focus. This prevents speaking to the wrong site after switching. See [Talk to people on site](#talk-down).

lane-lifecycle.title: Lane states and lifecycle
lane-lifecycle.summary: Every state a lane can be in, what moves it between states, and who triggers each move.
lane-lifecycle.body:
A lane moves through a small, fixed set of states. The diagram shows every allowed transition; anything not drawn cannot happen.

{{diagram:lane-lifecycle}}

## States

| State | What it means | What you see |
|---|---|---|
| Free | No incident. The next take or raise uses the first free letter. | Dashed slot in the rail. |
| Focused | The lane is in the workspace. Unattended time stays at zero. A new lane opens here, with the video connecting for about 2 s. | Full workspace, colored lane strip. |
| Peripheral | Open but not on screen. Unattended time counts up. | Card in the rail with a meter. |
| Escalated | Peripheral for 45 s (warning) or 60 s (supervisor paged). | Amber or red bar under the top bar; red card. |
| Closing | Closeout dialog open. The lane is still live and the ladder keeps running. | Three-step dialog. |
| Hand-off requested | Waiting for the supervisor to accept. Still yours. | Timeline entry, lane stays open. |
| Closed | Record sealed, lane free again. | Confirmation; record in History. |

## Transitions

| From → to | Trigger | By |
|---|---|---|
| Free → Focused | Take next ([[T]]) or Raise incident ([[I]]) | Operator |
| Focused → Peripheral | You switch to another lane or a camera | Operator |
| Peripheral → Escalated | 45 s, then 60 s without attention | System |
| Peripheral or Escalated → Focused | Press the lane letter or select its card | Operator |
| Escalated → Escalated (acknowledged) | [[K]] Acknowledge | Operator |
| Focused → Closing | [[E]] Close incident | Operator |
| Closing → Focused | Cancel or [[Esc]] | Operator |
| Closing → Closed → Free | Close incident in step 2 | Operator, then system |
| Focused → Hand-off requested → Free | Hand off, then supervisor accepts | Operator, then supervisor |

> [!NOTE]
> The response ladder runs inside the lane in every open state, including Peripheral and Closing. See [Response ladder stages](#ladder-stages).

queue-priority.title: Queue order and priorities
queue-priority.summary: How alarms are ranked, what P1 to P4 mean, and why the order is fixed.
queue-priority.body:
## Priorities

| Priority | Meaning | Typical example |
|---|---|---|
| {{prio:P1}} Critical | A person inside a protected line, forced entry. | Person at a rear door after hours. |
| {{prio:P2}} High | Likely intrusion or safety risk. | Vehicle idling at a loading bay after close. |
| {{prio:P3}} Medium | Needs a look, low immediate risk. | Person photographing a gate. |
| {{prio:P4}} Low | Probably benign or technical. | Allow-listed delivery; view obstructed. |

The model proposes the priority from the factors listed in the lane's **Why** box, for example after hours, line crossed, plate not on the allow-list, loitering time. Model confidence is one factor, not the verdict.

## Order

The queue is sorted by **priority first**, then by **wait time**, longest first. The order is the same for every operator on the desk, so two people never argue about what is next.

You can take a specific alarm out of order (select it, then [[T]]). The timeline records how long it waited.

> [!TIP]
> Filter **P1–P2** during a busy period to see only what cannot wait. Filtering hides items; it never reorders them.

attention-model.title: Attention and escalation
attention-model.summary: How the console measures attention on each lane and when it asks for help.
attention-model.body:
An open lane that no one is looking at is a risk. The console measures **unattended time** for each lane and escalates in steps, following alarm-management practice (ISA-18.2): warn early, escalate only when needed, and never let an alarm disappear.

{{diagram:attention}}

## What counts as attention

A lane is attended while it is the focused lane, the console window is visible and the console is not locked. Everything else counts: another lane in focus, a camera view, the lock screen, or the console window hidden behind another application. A dialog over the focused lane (for example the closeout dialog) does not stop attention on that lane.

## The steps

| Unattended | Level | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| 0–29 s | Normal | Meter fills quietly on the lane card. |
| 30 s | Notice | Meter and card turn amber. |
| 45 s | Warning | Amber bar under the top bar with a countdown to 01:00. |
| 60 s | Alarm | Red bar, supervisor paged, message, logo dot turns red. Counted in the shift report. |

## Clearing

Looking at the lane resets its time to zero. **Acknowledge** ([[K]]) tells the supervisor you know about the lane but does not reset it; the bar stays until you look.

> [!NOTE]
> The desk you chose at sign-in decides which supervisor is paged.

ladder-stages.title: Response ladder stages
ladder-stages.summary: The four escalation steps each incident follows and the timing between them.
ladder-stages.body:
The ladder turns a site's response procedure into a timed sequence. It makes sure an incident keeps moving even if the operator is busy elsewhere, and it records every step.

{{diagram:ladder}}

## Rules

- The ladder starts at **Talk-down** the moment a lane opens.
- Each step has a timer. When it runs out, the next step starts by itself.
- **Halt** ([[H]]) freezes the timer; **Resume** ([[R]]) continues it.
- **Siren** arms the site siren automatically.
- **Keyholder** queues a call to the site's contact list.
- **Dispatch** never starts on its own. It waits for **Confirm dispatch**.
- For P3 and P4 incidents, Dispatch is shown dimmed as a reminder that it is rarely right.
- Closing the incident ends the ladder wherever it is.

> [!NOTE]
> Step timings are set per site in the site procedure. The values shown here (30 s, 45 s, 60 s) are the defaults.

video-states.title: Video stream states
video-states.summary: Live, connecting, degraded and lost streams, and what still works in each.
video-states.body:
| State | What you see | What still works |
|---|---|---|
| Connecting | Spinner: "Connecting to CAM …". Lasts about 2 s after a lane opens. | Everything except the picture. |
| Live | Picture with LIVE and the time top right; quality bottom right (for example 1080p · 12 fps · 140 ms). | Everything. |
| Degraded | Amber **DEGRADED** label, for example 3 fps · 900 ms. | Everything; the picture lags. Allow for the delay before you speak. |
| Lost | "Stream lost" with a countdown to the next reconnect and **Retry now**. | Speaker and siren: they use a separate link. |

{{fig:stream-lost}}

The console retries a lost stream by itself. When the picture returns, the timeline records **Stream restored**; when quality returns, it records **Stream quality restored**.

> [!NOTE]
> A lost stream on one camera is a camera problem. If every video freezes at once, the console has probably lost its connection. See [Connection lost](#connection-lost).

camera-states.title: Camera states
camera-states.summary: Live, motion, fault and offline: what each camera mark means.
camera-states.body:
Each camera has one state. The mark's shape differs as well as its color, so the states stay readable for color-blind operators and on a monochrome display.

| Mark | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| {{dot:live}} | Live | Streaming normally. |
| {{dot:motion}} | Motion | Analytics see movement below the alarm threshold. No alarm has fired. |
| {{dot:fault}} | Fault | Streaming, but degraded: low frame rate or high latency. Flagged to maintenance. |
| {{dot:offline}} | Offline | No signal. Speaker and deterrents on that device may be unavailable. |

Motion and faults are listed first on the camera wall because they are the ones worth a look.

session-states.title: Session and connection states
session-states.summary: Signed out, active, locked and offline: what each means and how to move between them.
session-states.body:
Your session and the network connection each have a small set of states.

{{diagram:session}}

## Session

| State | How you get there | How you leave |
|---|---|---|
| Signed out | Start of shift, or Sign out with no lanes open. | Sign in. |
| Active | Sign in, or Unlock. | Lock, or Sign out. |
| Locked | **Lock screen** from the command palette, or automatically after 10 minutes without input **when no lane is open**. | Unlock with your password. |

The console never locks itself while a lane is open: an unattended incident is more dangerous than an unlocked screen in a staffed control room.

## Connection

| State | What happens |
|---|---|
| Online | Normal. |
| Offline | A blue bar explains what is paused. Taking alarms, talk-down, siren, strobe, raise and dispatch are blocked with a message. Timers keep running on the server. The console retries by itself; **Retry now** tries at once. |

When the connection returns, a message confirms how long it was down and that lanes, queue and notes were re-synced.

keyboard-shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
keyboard-shortcuts.summary: Every key in the console. Press Shift+? to see them on screen.
keyboard-shortcuts.body:
Single-key shortcuts work anywhere except while you type in a field. Deterrents need a 600 ms hold, so a stray press never fires a siren.

{{fig:keyboard-sheet}}

## Lanes

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| [[A]] [[B]] [[C]] | Focus lane A, B or C |
| [[T]] | Take the next alarm (or the selected one) |
| [[E]] | Close the focused incident |
| [[F]] | Focus mode on or off |
| [[K]] | Acknowledge an unattended-lane escalation |
| [[N]] | Jump to the note field |

## Deterrence

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| [[Space]] (hold) | Talk to the site; release to stop |
| [[S]] (hold 600 ms) | Arm the siren; press again to stop |
| [[L]] (hold 600 ms) | Arm the strobe; press again to stop |
| [[M]] | Move the microphone to the lane or camera on screen |
| [[H]] / [[R]] | Halt / resume the response ladder |

## Navigate

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| [[Ctrl+K]] or [[⌘+K]] | Command palette |
| [[/]] | Search History |
| [[W]] | Camera wall |
| [[P]] | Shift report |
| [[,]] | Settings |
| [[I]] | Raise an incident (camera view) |
| [[Shift+?]] | Keyboard sheet |
| [[F1]] | Help for what is on screen |
| [[Esc]] | Close the dialog, drawer or camera view |

## In dialogs

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| [[Ctrl+Enter]] | Closeout memo: go to next steps |
| [[↑]] [[↓]] [[Enter]] | Command palette: move and run |
| [[←]] [[→]] | Record tabs and settings options |

## In Help

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| [[/]] | Search help |
| [[↑]] [[↓]] | Move in the contents tree |
| [[→]] [[←]] | Open or close a section |
| [[Esc]] | Close a figure, clear the search, or close Help |

command-palette.title: Command palette
command-palette.summary: Run any command, jump to a lane or site, or open a help article by typing.
command-palette.body:
The command palette finds anything by name. It is the fastest way to reach commands that have no key of their own.

{{fig:command-palette}}

1. Press [[Ctrl+K]] ([[⌘+K]] on a Mac), or select the search box in the top bar.
2. Type part of a command, lane, site or help topic.
3. Use [[↑]] [[↓]] to move, [[Enter]] to run, [[Esc]] to close.

## Groups

| Group | Contains |
|---|---|
| Lanes | Go to an open lane, take next, close, focus mode |
| Deterrence | Move mic, halt or resume the ladder |
| View | Camera wall, theme, typeface, settings, keyboard sheet, shift report, history, lock screen, sign out |
| Help | Open Help, or any help article by its title |
| Sites | Open a site in the estate tree |
| Simulate | Prototype only: escalation, degraded or lost stream, quiet shift, connection lost |

status-colors.title: Colors, marks and badges
status-colors.summary: What every color, mark and badge in the console means.
status-colors.body:
Color is never the only signal: every state also has a shape, an icon or a word.

## Status colors

| Color | Means | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Red | Critical: act now | {{prio:P1}}, supervisor paged, camera fault, siren on |
| Orange | High | {{prio:P2}} |
| Amber | Warning: act soon | {{prio:P3}}, unattended 30–59 s, motion, ladder halted |
| Blue | Information | {{prio:P4}}, dispatched, connection lost bar |
| Green | OK, done | Live camera, resolved, connection restored |

## Lane colors

Each lane letter keeps one color for as long as it is open: {{lane:A}} {{lane:B}} {{lane:C}}. The same color marks the lane in the workspace edge, cards, the tree and the camera wall.

## Logo dot

| Dot | Desk state |
|---|---|
| Blue | Idle: no lanes open |
| Amber | At least one lane open |
| Red, pulsing | A lane unattended for 60 s |
| Grey | Offline |

## Record badges

{{badge:b-ok|RESOLVED}} {{badge:b-info|REFERRED}} {{badge:b-neu|FALSE ALARM}}

settings.title: Settings
settings.summary: Theme and typeface for this workstation.
settings.body:
Open Settings with [[,]], the gear icon in the top bar (in the rail on a laptop), or **Settings** in the bottom bar on a tablet.

{{fig:settings}}

## Theme

- **Dark** is the control-room default: less glare in a dim room, and video stands out.
- **Light** is for daylight desks.

## Typeface

| Option | Choose it for |
|---|---|
| IBM Plex Sans + Mono | Default. Compact and neutral. |
| Inter + JetBrains Mono | A familiar interface font with tall digits. |
| Atkinson Hyperlegible | The clearest I, l, 1 and 0, O. Easier on long shifts and for low vision. |

Changes apply at once to the whole console, timers and camera codes included, and stay on this workstation.

glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.summary: Terms used in the console and in this help.
glossary.body:
| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Alarm | A detection from a camera or sensor that waits in the queue until someone takes it. |
| Incident | An alarm someone has taken, or a situation raised from a camera. Lives in a lane until closed. |
| Lane | One open incident, named A, B or C. See [Lanes: the three-lane model](#three-lanes). |
| Focused lane | The lane in the workspace. |
| Peripheral lane | An open lane shown as a card in the right rail. |
| Unattended time | How long a lane has gone without being on screen. |
| Escalation | The warning at 45 s and the supervisor page at 60 s of unattended time. |
| Acknowledge | Telling the supervisor you know about an unattended lane, without switching to it. |
| Response ladder | The four timed steps of a site's response: talk-down, siren, keyholder, dispatch. |
| Halt | Freezing the ladder timer while you handle the incident. |
| Talk-down | Speaking to people on site through the camera speaker. |
| Deterrent | Talk-down, siren or strobe. |
| Keyholder | The site's contact person, called at ladder step 3. |
| Dispatch | A request for police attendance. Never automatic. |
| Closeout memo | The text the site owner reads about what happened and how it ended. At least 40 characters. |
| Outcome | Resolved, False alarm or Referred to police. |
| Record | A sealed, read-only copy of a closed incident, kept for 90 days. |
| Camera view | Watching a camera without an incident. |
| Site log | Where speech, deterrents and notes from camera view are written. |
| Watch score | A 0–100 measure of unusual activity at a site. |
| Desk | Your workstation position; decides which supervisor is paged. |

lane-limit.title: Lane limit reached
lane-limit.summary: You tried to take or raise a fourth incident while three lanes are open.
lane-limit.body:
**What you see:** a red **Lane limit reached · 3 of 3** box above the queue, or a message after **Raise incident**.

{{fig:lane-limit}}

**Why:** a fourth lane is refused by design. See [Lanes: the three-lane model](#three-lanes).

## What to do

1. Decide which open lane can end or move. Usually the lowest priority, or the one nearest to resolution.
2. Either **close** it ([[E]]) or **hand it off** to the supervisor.
3. Take the waiting alarm with [[T]].

Select **Dismiss** to hide the box without changing anything.

> [!TIP]
> If a new P1 arrives while you are full and nothing can end, hand off the lowest-priority lane. The supervisor sees the hand-off request at once.

stream-problems.title: Video is slow, frozen or lost
stream-problems.summary: What to do when a camera stream degrades or drops.
stream-problems.body:
## Degraded

**What you see:** an amber **DEGRADED** label and a low frame rate.

- Keep working. Allow for the delay before you speak or judge movement.
- If quality does not return within a minute, note it: "Stream degraded, 3 fps".

## Lost

**What you see:** **Stream lost** with a reconnect countdown.

1. Wait for the automatic retry, or select **Retry now**.
2. The speaker and siren use a separate link: you can still talk down and arm the siren.
3. If the stream stays down, open another camera on the same site from **Site cameras** in camera view, or from the camera wall.

## Every video froze at once

That is a connection problem, not a camera problem. See [Connection lost](#connection-lost).

sign-in-problems.title: Cannot sign in
sign-in-problems.summary: Errors on the sign-in screen and how to fix them.
sign-in-problems.body:
{{fig:sign-in-error}}

| Message | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Enter your operator ID or email. | The ID field is empty. | Type your ID, for example OP-214. |
| Enter your password. | The password field is empty. | Type your password. |
| That operator ID and password don't match. N attempts left… | Wrong ID or password. | Check Caps Lock (a warning shows under the field), use the eye button to see what you typed, try again. |
| Account locked | Five failed attempts. The account locks for 15 minutes. | Ask the desk supervisor to unlock it now, or wait. |

## Forgot your password

The console has no self-service reset. Ask the desk supervisor; they reset it and give you a temporary password.

> [!NOTE]
> Prototype: any password signs in; type **wrong** to see the error, five times to see the lock.

lock-screen.title: Console locked
lock-screen.summary: Why the console locks, what keeps running, and how to unlock it.
lock-screen.body:
The lock screen hides the console while you are away from the desk. Lanes, timers and the queue keep running behind it.

{{fig:lock-screen}}

## Why it locked

- You chose **Lock screen** in the command palette, or
- nobody touched the keyboard or mouse for **10 minutes** and **no lane was open**. The console never locks itself with a lane open.

## Unlock

1. Type your password.
2. Select **Unlock** or press [[Enter]].

You return exactly where you were.

## While locked

The **While you're away** box lists open lanes with their unattended time and the number of alarms waiting. Unattended time keeps counting, and the supervisor is still paged at 01:00.

## Someone else needs the desk

Select **Sign in as another operator**. This works only when no lanes are open: hand off or close them first.

connection-lost.title: Connection lost
connection-lost.summary: The console lost its link to the server. What is paused, what keeps running, and what to do.
connection-lost.body:
**What you see:** a blue **Connection lost** bar under the top bar with the time offline. Video is greyed out and marked **Paused · offline**. The logo dot turns grey.

{{fig:connection-lost}}

## What is paused

Taking alarms, talk-down, siren, strobe, raising incidents and dispatch. Trying one shows **Offline · not sent**: nothing is queued to fire later.

## What keeps running

- Lane timers and the response ladder, on the server.
- Supervisor paging for unattended lanes.
- Notes you type: kept on this workstation and sent when the connection returns.

## What to do

1. Wait: the console retries by itself. Select **Retry now** to try at once.
2. If it lasts more than 30 seconds, call the desk supervisor on the phone. They can see your lanes and take over.
3. Check the network cable or Wi-Fi of this workstation.

When the link returns, a message shows how long it was down; lanes, queue and notes are re-synced.

> [!TIP]
> Prototype: run **Simulate: connection lost** from the command palette to see the state for 8 seconds.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.summary: Short answers to questions operators ask most.
faq.body:
### Why can't the console dispatch police by itself?

Dispatch has legal and cost consequences for the client, and false dispatches erode police response. A person decides. See [Run the response ladder](#response-ladder).

### Why is a fourth lane refused?

Beyond three parallel incidents, operators miss changes in peripheral video. See [Lanes: the three-lane model](#three-lanes).

### I pressed S and nothing happened.

The siren needs a 600 ms **hold**. Press and keep holding until the button reads ON.

### I spoke, but the site didn't hear me.

The microphone may be on another lane. The dock at the bottom says where it is. Press [[M]] to move it.

### Why did the supervisor get paged? I was busy in another lane.

A lane counts as unattended whenever it is not on screen, whatever you are doing elsewhere. Glance at it by pressing its letter, or press [[K]] to acknowledge. See [Attention and escalation](#attention-model).

### Can I edit an incident after closing it?

No. Records are sealed. A supervisor can add an addendum. See [History and incident records](#incident-records).

### Where did the siren go when I left the camera?

Deterrents started in camera view stop when you leave that camera. Raise an incident first if they need to keep running. See [Watch a camera without an incident](#camera-view).

### Help doesn't open.

Help is loaded the first time you open it. If the network is down, Help shows **Help could not load** with **Try again**. The console keeps working without it.

ladder.alt: Response ladder with four steps. Talk-down lasts 30 seconds, then Siren, which arms the siren and lasts 45 seconds, then Keyholder, which queues a call and lasts 60 seconds, then Dispatch, which waits for the operator and never starts on its own.
ladder.caption: Default timings. Halt (H) freezes the current step; Resume (R) continues it.

session.alt: Two state diagrams. Session: Signed out goes to Active on sign in; Active goes to Locked on lock or after 10 idle minutes with no lanes; Locked returns to Active on unlock; Active returns to Signed out on sign out when no lanes are open. Connection: Online goes to Offline when the link drops; Offline returns to Online when it reconnects.
session.caption: Session states (left) and connection states (right). They are independent: a locked console can also be offline.
